claims.text: High-entropy alloys contain multiple principal elements.
Increasing the levels of passivating elements such as Al and Cr in an HEA will promote formation of a protective oxide layer.
Al- and Cr-containing alloys can form compact, self-healing alumina and chromia layers, respectively.
The proposed HEA will sustain a continuous, robust, self-healing oxide film under simultaneous elevated temperature, corrosion, and mechanical wear.
The proposed HEA will rapidly regenerate its protective oxide layer during operation.
High configurational entropy promotes rapid in situ formation of protective oxide or passivation films.
Protective alumina or chromia films act as diffusion barriers against further oxidation and corrosion.
The protective oxide film reduces exposure of the underlying metal to mechanical wear.
Conventional structural alloys degrade rapidly under combined high-temperature tribo-corrosion because their protective oxides are inadequate or unstable.
Protective oxide layers on structural alloys can be unstable in molten fluoride salts, leading to selective dissolution, wall thinning, and possible loss of structural integrity.
An Al- and Cr-containing HEA can have a lower high-temperature molten-salt corrosion rate than a conventional structural alloy.
The proposed HEA will have a significantly lower tribo-corrosion rate than conventional structural alloys under combined thermal, corrosive, and mechanical loading.
Conventional structural alloys lacking optimized self-healing oxide formation typically have higher degradation rates under comparable conditions.
The magnitude of improvement depends on passivating-element concentration, microstructure, and operating conditions.
